title: Fed Decision in September?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's September 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for September 15-16, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their September meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent U.S. employment data showing stronger-than-expected job gains have supported arguments for tighter policy at the September 15-16 FOMC meeting, while moderating inflation readings and cooling core measures have kept a hold in contention. Persistent price pressures above the 2% target, elevated energy costs tied to geopolitical tensions, and divided signals from prior FOMC votes have left traders balanced between the two leading outcomes. Upcoming August CPI and PPI releases will likely determine whether momentum shifts toward a 25-basis-point increase or reinforces the case for no change, as officials have signaled a data-dependent stance ahead of updated projections.

title: US Open ATP: Zizou Bergs vs Botic van de Zandschulp
description:
This market refers to the tennis match between Zizou Bergs and Botic van de Zandschulp in the US Open ATP, originally scheduled for September 5, 2026 at 11:00AM ET.

This market will resolve to 'Zizou Bergs' if Zizou Bergs advances against Botic van de Zandschulp.

This market will resolve to 'Botic van de Zandschulp' if Botic van de Zandschulp advances against Zizou Bergs.

If the match is canceled (not played at all), ends in a tie, or a winner has not been determined by September 19, 2026, 11:59 PM ET (14 days after the scheduled start), this market will resolve to 50-50.

If the match ends in a walkover (player withdraws before the start and the other advances automatically), this market will resolve to 50-50.

The primary resolution source will be official information from the ATP Tour. A consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: Zizou Bergs enters this US Open third-round clash as the higher-ranked player at No. 37 and seeded No. 31, while Botic van de Zandschulp sits at No. 70. Van de Zandschulp's straight-sets upset of sixth seed Alex de Minaur in round two has injected significant momentum, marking his third appearance in the US Open round of 32 and highlighting his proven hard-court resilience and prior Grand Slam quarterfinal experience. Bergs reached this stage by defeating Jesper de Jong in four sets after a mixed hard-court summer. With no prior head-to-head record, the matchup pits Bergs' current ranking edge against van de Zandschulp's recent breakthrough form on the outdoor hard courts in New York.

title: Next French Presidential Election
description:
The next French presidential election is currently expected to be held around April 2027.  This market pertains to the outcome of the next French presidential election, regardless of whether it follows the scheduled end of the current term or is held earlier. 

The President of France is elected via a two-round system; a candidate must secure over 50% of the vote to win outright in the first round. If no candidate achieves this, the top two contenders advance to a runoff.

This market will resolve according to the candidate who wins this election.

This market includes any potential second round. If, for any reason, the results of the election are not known by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the French Government, specifically the Ministry of the Interior (https://www.interieur.gouv.fr/).

The President of France is elected via a two-round system; a candidate must secure over 50% of the vote to win outright in the first round. If no candidate achieves this, the top two contenders advance to a runoff.

This market will resolve according to the candidate who wins this election.

This market includes any potential second round. If, for any reason, the results of the election are not known by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the French Government, specifically the Ministry of the Interior (https://www.interieur.gouv.fr/).

The President of France is elected via a two-round system; a candidate must secure over 50% of the vote to win outright in the first round. If no candidate achieves this, the top two contenders advance to a runoff.

This market will resolve according to the candidate who wins this election.

This market includes any potential second round. If, for any reason, the results of the election are not known by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the French Government, specifically the Ministry of the Interior (https://www.interieur.gouv.fr/).

eventMetadata.context_description: Marine Le Pen maintains the highest trader-implied probability in this market due to consistent first-round polling leads of 33-36 percent and strong projected runoff margins against most rivals, bolstered by her recent legal clearance to stand. Édouard Philippe ranks second as the leading centrist contender, though a crowded field of moderates including Gabriel Attal, Raphaël Glucksmann, Bruno Retailleau, and François Hollande fragments that vote and raises the chance of a Le Pen-Mélenchon runoff. Mélenchon's recent polling surge to the mid-teens has lifted his odds by positioning him to qualify in multiple scenarios. The two-round system, scheduled for April 2027, amplifies these dynamics, with upcoming debates and candidate consolidation moves likely to influence further shifts in the closely contested probabilities reflected by trader consensus.

title: 2026 Men’s US Open Winner (Tennis)
description:
The 2026 U.S. Open tennis tournament is scheduled for August 23 - September 13, 2026.

This market will resolve to the player that wins the 2026 U.S. Open Men’s Singles Tournament.

If at any point it becomes impossible for a listed player to win the 2026 U.S. Open Men’s Singles Tournament per the rules of the tournament, the corresponding market will resolve to “No”.

If the 2026 U.S. Open Men’s Singles Tournament is cancelled, postponed after October 31, 2026, or there is otherwise no winner declared within that timeframe, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source will be official information from the U.S. Open (https://www.usopen.org/index.html); however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: Carlos Alcaraz leads the market at 49% implied probability as the defending champion who has advanced comfortably to the fourth round after returning from a four-month wrist injury layoff, winning his opening matches in straight sets and reporting strong recovery. Alexander Zverev sits second at 21.7% on the strength of his seeding and consistent hard-court results, while Ben Shelton at 8.1% benefits from home-crowd support and a solid third-round win. Daniil Medvedev holds 6.1% after a straight-sets victory, with the field remaining competitive as several top seeds have already exited and the bracket opens further. Recent third-round results, including upsets such as Taylor Fritz’s loss to Francisco Cerundolo, have reinforced the current pricing based on verified match outcomes and player form.

eventMetadata.context_description: J.D. Vance and Robert F. Kennedy Jr. remain locked in a tight contest for the 2028 Republican presidential nomination, with trader consensus pricing each near 50 percent amid substantial uncertainty more than two years out. Vance benefits from his position as vice president and visibility in the current administration, while Kennedy draws support through cabinet service and appeal to overlapping voter coalitions. Marco Rubio holds a distant third at 20 percent, reflecting his role as secretary of state but less dominant positioning in early polling averages. The compressed spread between the leaders stems from the extended timeline, limited formal announcements, and potential for shifts tied to 2026 midterm results, administration policy outcomes, and eventual endorsements. Recent polls show Vance ahead nationally but with narrowing gaps in key states, underscoring how mid-cycle developments could widen separation among contenders.

eventMetadata.context_description: Salahdine Parnasse entered his UFC debut as a heavily favored lightweight prospect against veteran Dan Hooker, with traders pricing the French fighter as a strong favorite due to his undefeated recent streak, multiple KSW titles across weight classes, and home-country support at Accor Arena in Paris. Hooker, at 36 and coming off consecutive losses including a submission defeat, faced stylistic challenges against Parnasse’s forward pressure, body-kick accuracy, and finishing power, despite the New Zealander’s experience and reach advantage. Pre-fight reports highlighted Parnasse’s recent form and promotional newcomer momentum as key drivers of the implied probability gap, while noting Hooker’s history of competitive bouts against top lightweights. The bout’s early resolution aligned with market positioning around striking exchanges and conditioning edges.

title: UEFA Champions League: 2027 Champion
description:
This market will resolve according to the team that wins the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League Championship.

If at any point it becomes impossible for a listed team to win the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League Championship per the rules of UEFA Champions League (e.g., they are eliminated in the playoffs), the corresponding market will resolve to "No".

If the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League season is cancelled, postponed after June 19, 2027, 11:59 PM ET or there is otherwise no winner declared within that timeframe, this market will resolve to "Other".

The primary resolution source will be official information from UEFA Champions League; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: The 2026-27 UEFA Champions League league phase is just beginning, leaving the title race exceptionally open with trader consensus reflecting broad parity among elite clubs and a 50% probability on "Other." Arsenal, Bayern Munich, Barcelona, Paris Saint-Germain, and Real Madrid sit at the front of the listed options on the back of strong domestic campaigns, deep squads reinforced by summer transfers, and recent deep European runs, yet none exceeds 17.5% implied probability. Factors such as Mikel Arteta’s side reaching last season’s final, PSG’s bid for a historic three-peat under Luis Enrique, Bayern’s attacking firepower with Harry Kane, Barcelona’s La Liga dominance, and Real Madrid’s experience keep the field tightly bunched, while injuries, fixture congestion, and the expanded format’s unpredictability sustain realistic paths for several additional contenders.

eventMetadata.context_description: The Rays enter as the stronger side with an 84-57 record atop the AL East, powered by Drew Rasmussen’s 14-5 mark and 2.95 ERA, while the Rangers sit at 70-72 and second in the AL West behind Jacob deGrom’s 10-9, 4.00 ERA start. Multiple Rangers arms remain on the injured list, including Nathan Eovaldi and several relievers, limiting depth against Tampa Bay’s disciplined lineup featuring Yandy Díaz and Junior Caminero. The series split the prior two games, with the Rays winning the most recent 7-6 contest at Globe Life Field. Home-field factors and deGrom’s occasional dominance create competitive balance, but the Rays’ overall roster health and recent form shape the current trader consensus reflected in market pricing.

This market will resolve to "Oregon" if Oregon outscore Boise State by 16 or more points in the second half.

Otherwise, this market will resolve to "Boise State".

Only points scored during that period count; overtime is not included.

If the game is postponed, this market will remain open until the game has been completed. If the game is canceled entirely, with no make-up game, this market will resolve 50-50.

eventMetadata.context_description: Oregon entered the season opener as heavy favorites at No. 2 in the rankings, with quarterback Dante Moore returning for a final year after throwing for over 3,500 yards and 30 touchdowns in 2025, supported by a top-tier defense and roster depth under coach Dan Lanning. Boise State, transitioning into the rebuilt Pac-12 after multiple conference titles and a playoff appearance in 2024, brought back quarterback Maddux Madsen and a capable rushing attack, aiming to build on prior competitive showings against the Ducks. Pre-game trader consensus reflected Oregon’s home dominance at Autzen Stadium and talent edge, though historical results showed Boise State capable of close contests on the road. The matchup highlighted Oregon’s offensive line turnover concerns and Boise State’s potential for early leads in a high-stakes nonconference test.

eventMetadata.context_description: Fluminense and Vasco da Gama meet in a tightly contested Rio derby for the Brasileirão, with both sides showing recent momentum that underpins the near-even trader pricing. Fluminense sits fourth with 42 points and remains unbeaten in four matches under Marcão, who stabilized the side after the Copa do Brasil exit, though key absences including a rested Thiago Silva ahead of the Libertadores add uncertainty. Vasco, fighting near the relegation zone, arrives with three positive results in a row and renewed confidence under Pedro Emanuel despite missing attackers like Brenner. The recent 3-1 Copa do Brasil win by Vasco and the clubs’ head-to-head intensity further balance expectations for a competitive encounter at the Maracanã.
